suggestion: Select and connect one primary sportsbook odds feed to obtain authoritative opening and closing lines for CLV.
rationale: CLV is the skill metric; it cannot be computed without a real, timestamped line feed. This is the highest-value missing piece.
impact: High — unlocks the core skill-measurement gate for every strategy.

suggestion: Confirm an automatable official stats endpoint (team + player) and document its update cadence.
rationale: Projection models need stable, refreshable stats; an undocumented feed is a single point of failure.

suggestion: Add a depth-chart update monitor that flags when a starter is ruled out and names the elevating backup automatically.
rationale: Converts the injury + depth cross-reference into a live, no-manual-input signal for deficiency detection.
impact: High — directly satisfies the backup-replacement tracking requirement.

suggestion: Standardize CLV as the primary ranking metric and win-rate as a secondary, clearly-labeled variance metric.
rationale: Removing luck requires ranking on CLV, not short-term win rate; labeling win-rate as variance prevents misreading.
impact: High — aligns the leaderboard with the skill goal.

suggestion: Build a correlation matrix across market types (side, total, player props) before permitting multi-leg parlay/prop combos.
rationale: Correlated legs inflate or misstate edge; a computed correlation matrix is required to build valid combos.
impact: High — de-risks parlay and prop-combo strategies.

suggestion: Add a selectivity gate that ranks strategies by conviction and caps the number of bets per slate.
rationale: Selectively skill-based strategies take fewer, higher-conviction bets; a cap enforces selectivity.
impact: Medium — reduces variance and focuses edge.

suggestion: Implement a rolling out-of-sample window (e.g., walk-forward) as a mandatory validation gate.
rationale: Walk-forward testing prevents overfitting and confirms edge persists on data the strategy has not seen.
impact: High — guards against luck/overfit strategies entering the leaderboard.

suggestion: Require a pre-declared CLV threshold and minimum bet count before a strategy is eligible for the leaderboard.
rationale: Pre-declared gates prevent post-hoc threshold tuning that manufactures apparent skill.

suggestion: Add a position-reconciliation rule and log every cross-source position discrepancy to the Flagged for Review page.
rationale: Real discrepancies (e.g., a player listed at C in the injury report but RG on the depth chart) must be resolved and logged, not silently merged.
impact: Medium — improves data integrity and reviewability.

suggestion: Quantify backup-replacement severity with a transparent, documented score rather than an assumed constant.
rationale: Severity must be computed from official injury + depth data; an assumed constant would be a hallucination.

suggestion: Surface a per-strategy status panel (eligible / pending gates / flagged) on the leaderboard so reviewers see why a strategy is ranked where it is.
rationale: Improves decision-making by making the validation state visible at a glance.
impact: Medium — directly serves the decision-support goal.

suggestion: Add a decision log that records which suggestion was chosen for each open question and the rationale, before implementation.
rationale: The user wants the best path chosen before changes; a decision log makes the choice auditable.

suggestion: Automate a nightly build + verification step that fails the build if any table row lacks a resolvable source link.
rationale: Enforces the no-hallucination rule structurally rather than by convention.
impact: High — guarantees the verification rule holds on every deploy.
